classification.difficultyReason: Use exact tangent values and intercepts to construct general-form equations; part c requires converting an angle measured from the vertical.

content.prompt: Determine the equation of each straight line sketched below in exact general form.

spec.description: Unshaded coordinate axes with a rising double-arrow line, y-intercept 4 and a 45° inclination annotation at its x-intercept. No grid.
spec.mathematics: The line is y=x+4. Its x-intercept is (-4,0), y-intercept is (0,4), and inclination is 45°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied axes, intercept and angle are visible; no equation or computed gradient is printed.

spec.description: Unshaded coordinate axes with a falling double-arrow line, y-intercept 4 and a 120° inclination annotation at the positive x-intercept. No grid.
spec.mathematics: The line is y=-sqrt(3)x+4. The inclination is the counterclockwise angle from the positive horizontal ray to the upper-left ray of the line.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied axes, intercept and angle are visible; no equation or computed gradient is printed.

spec.description: Unshaded coordinate axes with a falling double-arrow line crossing the x-axis at −6. At the y-intercept, a curved 30° marker joins the upward vertical ray and the upper-left ray of the line. No grid.
spec.mathematics: The inclination is 90°+30°=120°, so the gradient is -sqrt(3). The line passes through (-6,0). The unlabelled y-intercept remains unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied axes, x-intercept and vertical-reference angle are visible; the inclination, y-intercept value and equation are withheld.

answer.worked:
The marked angle is measured from the vertical.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=90^{\circ}+30^{\circ}\\\theta&=120^{\circ}\\m&=\tan120^{\circ}\\m&=-\sqrt3\\y-0&=-\sqrt3\bigl(x-(-6)\bigr)\\y&=-\sqrt3x-6\sqrt3\\\sqrt3x+y+6\sqrt3&=0\end{align*}$$
